title: Pączki: Rich Polish Jam-Filled Doughnuts
summary: A soft, yolk-rich yeast dough fried to a deep brown and filled with smooth jam.
equipment: 2 trays lined with floured baking paper
piping bag with a long narrow nozzle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Wake up the yeast
steps.text: Stir the yeast and 1 tsp of the sugar into the lukewarm milk and leave for 5-10 min until foamy on top.

steps.title: Beat the yolks
steps.text: Put the yolks, whole egg and the rest of the sugar in the mixer bowl and whisk for 3-4 min until thick and pale. Mix in the vanilla, salt and the yeasty milk. Beating air into the yolks lightens this heavy dough.

steps.title: Knead with the butter
steps.text: Fit the dough hook, add the flour and knead on low for 5 min. Add the soft butter a spoonful at a time, then knead on medium for 10-12 min until glossy, very soft and coming away from the sides. The long kneading builds the structure needed to hold all that fat.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Shape into a ball, put it in the oiled bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1.5 h until doubled.

steps.title: Second rise
steps.text: Knock out the air, fold the dough over on itself a few times, cover again and leave for 30 min.

steps.title: Cut and prove
steps.text: Roll the dough out on a floured worktop to 1.5 cm thick and cut rounds with the cutter, rerolling the scraps once, to make 16. Set them on the floured trays, cover loosely and prove for 30-45 min until visibly puffy.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 2.5 cm of oil in the heavy pot to 175 °C. Fry 3 at a time for 2.5-3 min on each side, until a deep chestnut brown with a pale band around the middle; adjust the heat to stay between 170 and 180 °C. Drain on the paper. The centre of one should reach about 88 °C, or break it open to make sure the inside is cooked.

steps.title: Fill with jam
steps.text: When cool enough to handle, make a hole in the side of each with the skewer. Pipe in about 1 tbsp jam until it just shows at the opening, and dust with icing sugar if you like.

tips: Oil that is too hot browns the outside before the dense centre cooks; a common mistake is skipping the thermometer.
Proving on floured paper lets you lift the soft rounds into the oil without denting them.
Choose a smooth, seedless jam so it pipes easily.
Rose-petal jam is the classic Polish filling if you can find it.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten the day they are made. Keep filled pączki in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days and bring back to room temperature before eating.
